source_text:
Fragmentum in epistulam ad Philemonem (in catenis)
Phm
1,1 Ἐν πολλαῖς ἐπιστολαῖς ξένον τίθησι ῥῆμα τοῦ μέλλοντος εἰσάγεσθαι λόγου
κατασκευαστικόν, καὶ νῦν ἐπειδὴ ἔμελλεν ἀξιοῦν ὑπὲρ Ὀνησίμου τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ἀξίᾳ–
ἀξία δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ δεδέσθαι–, τὸ ἀξιόπιστον τῆς παρακλήσεως δείκνυσιν.
thought_title: Paul's chains as the ground of his appeal
orientation: Photius is explaining how Paul, in Philemon 1:1, prepares his request for Onesimus by first establishing his own standing, which is his imprisonment.
pass_a_gloss: In many letters he places an unusual word as preparation for the argument that is about to be introduced, and now, since he was about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus by his own standing—and his standing is being in chains—he shows the credibility of the appeal.

choices.why: The glossary fixes this rendering for the striking word Paul places at the opening.
The glossary requires this sense of serving to prepare the ground for the coming argument.
The glossary fixes this rendering for Paul's worth or standing, which consists in his imprisonment.
The glossary requires this rendering for Paul's imprisonment as the basis of his credibility.
The glossary fixes this rendering for the trustworthiness of Paul's appeal.
The glossary requires this rendering for Paul's request on behalf of Onesimus.

bible_refs.note: The fragment comments on Philemon 1:1, where Paul identifies himself as a prisoner of Christ Jesus.

pass_b_english: In many letters Paul places an unusual word as preparation for the argument he is about to introduce. Here too, since he was about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus, he does so on the basis of his own standing—and his standing is being in chains. In this way he shows the credibility of his appeal.

last_rejected.fix: In many letters Paul places an unusual word preparatory to the argument he is about to introduce.
last_rejected.ruling: κατασκευαστικόν means 'preparatory'; rendering as noun 'preparation' conveys same sense, not a major error.
